answer: Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 46% independent neighbours on the funding graph. Because the trellis calculation reruns each epoch, the velvet weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the quill settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 55 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. That is 10 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
